newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Down on soft demand, lower crudes.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Down on soft demand, lower crudes.

text.p: Singapore middle distillate prices were lower on Friday in an uneventful market marked by weak regional demand and softer crude values, traders said.
They said the market was focused on India's spot and term tenders for diesel and the term tender for kerosene.
India's tenders were expected to be awarded this evening.

Offers into the August 1997-March 1998 tender saw offers of between $1.17 and $1.38 per barrel above MidEast spot quotes for the 1.0-percent grade c-and-f west coast, and $1.93-$2.04 premiums to the east coast.
Traders said India was expected to take between 450,000 and 550,000 tonnes of gas oil in its spot tender for August, compared with 855,000 tonnes in July.

Vietnam took 213,000 tonnes of gas oil in its tender for third quarter delivery, up from 170,000 tonnes in the second quarter. The awarded levels indicated the steep backwardation in regional prices, traders said.
In the Singapore market, offers were seen as low as $21.75 per barrel free-on-board (fob) basis for July 21-25 and as high as $22.00. Buying interest remained absent.
Traders said Chinese buyers also remained aloof and were not indicating any bids.
But the market was optimistic that Indonesia's demand in August would help to support prices.
They also noted that as was seen in the prices awarded into Vietnam's tender, the contago market reflected better sentiment from September as buyers emerge to stock up for the winter season.
The effects of the current cuts in crude run at the Shell and Esso refineries in Singapore would also help to absorb excess supplies and prop up the weak prices again.
Swaps gas oil were also battered with July losing 25 cents per barrel to $21.90/$22.00, while August shaved off 30 cents to $22.50/$22.60.
Jet fuel also continued to slide with an offer seen at $24.00 per barrel, down from Thursday's deal of $24.25.
